QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_10

question.text: An SIA issuing a Limited Assurance conclusion on an Annual Impact Report uses which of the following phrasings?

answer.text: 'In our opinion, the Annual Impact Report presents truly and fairly the impact…' (positive assurance)
'We certify that the SROI ratio of 3.2:1 is accurate' (certification language)

'Nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the Annual Impact Report is not prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable SAS standards' (negative assurance)
'We guarantee the impact outcomes disclosed' (guarantee language)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Limited assurance is expressed in the NEGATIVE form — 'nothing has come to our attention…' — exactly as in standard assurance frameworks. Reasonable assurance uses the positive 'in our opinion' form. SIAs may NEVER use 'certify' or 'guarantee'. **The Trap:** Option A is reasonable-assurance wording. Options B and D are prohibited under the Chapter 8 Inherent Limitation clause which explicitly states the report is not a certification or guarantee. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same negative/positive-assurance dichotomy in III-A / III-C Compliance, XV Research Analyst (report disclaimers) and standard assurance engagements. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Keep a template library: one engagement = one conclusion paragraph. Never draft conclusion wording freehand — peer review rejects 9 out of 10 custom phrasings.
